explore_lenses.label: How are key stakeholders responding?
explore_lenses.title: Unionists stress consent; others see risks or opportunity
explore_lenses.summary: The immediate responses are not a simple partisan split: unionist leaders emphasize Northern Irish self-determination, while some nationalist figures welcomed the sentiment. UK officials characterize the referendum threshold as unmet.

claims.text: DUP leader Gavin Robinson said Northern Ireland’s constitutional future must be decided by its people—not commentary from London, Dublin, or Washington—and said he expected Northern Ireland to continue choosing the UK.
Colum Eastwood, an SDLP MP and former party leader, responded positively to Trump’s remarks on social media, according to reporting by The Guardian.
Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch called Trump’s comments deeply unhelpful, arguing that loose statements about democratic countries’ futures create unnecessary tension.
The Good Friday Agreement protects the right of people in Northern Ireland to identify as British, Irish, or both, a safeguard central to why constitutional rhetoric is sensitive.

sections.heading: Consent Rules Govern Irish Unity
sections.body: The Belfast/Good Friday Agreement provides the constitutional framework for Northern Ireland, resting on the principle of consent and supporting power-sharing and UK-Ireland cooperation. It also protects the right of people in Northern Ireland to identify as British, Irish or both. Under Schedule 1 of the Northern Ireland Act 1998, the UK secretary of state may order a border poll and must do so if it appears likely that a majority would favor leaving the UK and joining a united Ireland; constitutional change also requires a majority in the South.

sections.heading: Political Leaders Split on Trump Remarks
sections.body: DUP leader Gavin Robinson said Northern Ireland’s constitutional future must be decided by its people, not by commentary from London, Dublin or Washington, and said he expected voters to continue choosing the UK. Colum Eastwood, an SDLP MP and former party leader, responded positively on social media, according to The Guardian. Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch called Trump’s intervention deeply unhelpful, arguing that loose comments about democratic countries’ futures create unnecessary tension.

sections.heading: Referendum Timing Remains Unspecified
sections.body: Trump’s statement that unification will eventually happen was his forecast, not a finding or commitment by either government. The Northern Ireland Act does not set a fixed polling threshold or mandatory evidence test for deciding when a majority is “likely,” though it bars another poll for seven years after a poll held under the schedule.

explore_lenses.label: Why was Chuvalo’s first Ali fight so consequential?
explore_lenses.title: A defining Canadian sports event
explore_lenses.summary: Chuvalo’s 1966 loss to Muhammad Ali elevated him from a respected domestic champion to a national symbol of endurance. The bout also brought a politically fraught Ali fight to Toronto during controversy over Ali’s opposition to the Vietnam War.

claims.text: Ali won a unanimous decision over Chuvalo after 15 rounds at Maple Leaf Gardens in Toronto on March 29, 1966; it was Ali’s first 15-round fight to go the distance.
The National Film Board of Canada describes the Toronto bout as a watershed in boxing history, while Canadian Press reporting said it made Chuvalo a Canadian hero despite the lopsided decision.
The fight was relocated to Canada after U.S. opposition to Ali’s antiwar stance disrupted a planned matchup with Ernie Terrell; Montreal then withdrew before Toronto hosted the event.

explore_lenses.label: Did “never knocked down” mean never stopped?
explore_lenses.title: An unusually durable—but not unbeaten—fighter
explore_lenses.summary: The distinction is important: Chuvalo was never knocked down in his professional career, but two fights were stopped before the final bell. His reputation rests on remaining upright against elite heavyweights rather than on having avoided every loss or stoppage.

claims.text: Canada’s Walk of Fame and the Ontario Sports Hall of Fame say Chuvalo was never knocked down in 93 professional bouts.
He lost by technical knockout to Joe Frazier in 1967 and George Foreman in 1970, yet reporting on his death says he was not knocked down in either fight.
Ali twice beat Chuvalo on decisions, in Toronto in 1966 and Vancouver in 1972; the Ontario Sports Hall of Fame records Ali’s view that Chuvalo was the toughest opponent he had fought.

explore_lenses.title: Public anti-drug advocacy after personal loss
explore_lenses.summary: Chuvalo’s public life after retirement included sustained anti-drug education work shaped by severe family losses. Canadian institutions recognized that work alongside his boxing achievements.

claims.text: The Governor General of Canada appointed Chuvalo a Member of the Order of Canada in 1998, citing his work speaking to young people, parents and educators about illegal-drug use after family tragedies.
Canada’s Sports Hall of Fame says he promoted Fight Against Drugs and gave lectures after losing family members to suicide and drug overdoses.
At a 2011 addiction-and-suicide gathering, Chuvalo told attendees that his family’s experience informed his warning to young people against tobacco, alcohol and drugs.

story_report.summary: George Chuvalo, the Canadian heavyweight boxer celebrated for extraordinary durability against opponents including Muhammad Ali and Joe Frazier, has died at 89. He was never knocked out, a defining record that helped make him a national sporting figure. His legacy also extended beyond boxing: after devastating losses in his family, Chuvalo became a prominent speaker warning young people and families about illegal-drug use.

sections.heading: Chuvalo’s defining bouts with Ali
sections.body: Ali defeated Chuvalo by unanimous decision after 15 rounds at Toronto’s Maple Leaf Gardens on March 29, 1966, in Ali’s first 15-round fight to go the distance. The bout reached Canada after opposition in the United States to Ali’s antiwar stance disrupted a planned fight with Ernie Terrell, and Montreal later withdrew as host. The National Film Board of Canada has described the Toronto contest as a watershed in boxing history, while Canadian Press reporting said it made Chuvalo a Canadian hero despite the lopsided decision.

sections.heading: Chuvalo’s record and public advocacy
sections.body: Canada’s Walk of Fame and the Ontario Sports Hall of Fame say Chuvalo was never knocked down in 93 professional bouts. He lost by technical knockout to Joe Frazier in 1967 and George Foreman in 1970, but reporting on his death said he was not knocked down in either fight; Ali also beat him on decisions in 1966 and 1972. Appointed a Member of the Order of Canada in 1998, Chuvalo spoke to young people, parents and educators about drug use after family tragedies and promoted Fight Against Drugs.

unresolved.text: Retrospective sources differ on whether Chuvalo’s professional career comprised 93 or 97 bouts, although they consistently report that he was never recorded as knocked down.
The reviewed reporting did not identify announced memorial arrangements or plans for continuing Chuvalo’s anti-drug program.

event_overview.title: About Iran War
event_overview.subject: Iran War
event_overview.summary: “Iran War” is a shorthand for the 2026 armed conflict centered on direct U.S.-Iran hostilities, Iranian attacks and alleged attacks involving states around the Persian Gulf, and disruptions to maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. The United States calls its campaign Operation Epic Fury and says it began to protect U.S. forces, regional partners and navigation; Iran has described the U.S. and Israeli actions as unlawful aggression.

facts.label: Start of direct U.S. operation
facts.value: U.S. Central Command says Operation Epic Fury against Iran began on February 28, 2026, at the President’s direction. In a March 10 letter to the UN Security Council, the United States said it had commenced combat operations on February 28 in cooperation with Israel.

facts.label: Parties and regional reach
facts.value: The conflict directly involves the United States and Iran, with the United States describing Israel as an ally in its initial operations. UN Security Council resolution 2817 (2026) addressed attacks attributed to Iran against Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Jordan.

facts.label: Strategic waterway
facts.value: The Strait of Hormuz lies between Iran and Oman and connects the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea. It is a major oil and liquefied-natural-gas transit chokepoint, so threats to shipping there can have wider energy-market effects.

facts.label: Competing legal positions
facts.value: The United States notified the Security Council that it was acting in self-defense under Article 51 of the UN Charter. Iran has told the Council that the U.S. and Israeli campaign constituted aggression and that subsequent Iranian measures were self-defense; these are opposing state positions, not a judicial determination.

facts.label: U.S. constitutional and statutory contex
facts.value: Under the War Powers Resolution, U.S. policy is that the collective judgment of Congress and the President should apply to the introduction and continued use of U.S. armed forces in hostilities; the statute identifies a declaration of war, specific statutory authorization, or a national emergency created by attack as bases for introducing forces into hostilities.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers a limited set of developments from July 22-27, 2026—military threats, congressional war-powers action, shipping and oil-market pressure, Houthi claims, and ceasefire diplomacy—not the conflict’s full origins, all operations, or its eventual outcome.

event_overview.title: About Russia-Ukraine War
event_overview.subject: Russia-Ukraine War
event_overview.summary: The Russia-Ukraine War is an armed conflict centered on Ukraine that grew from Russia's 2014 occupation of Crimea and fighting in eastern Ukraine into a full-scale Russian armed attack on 24 February 2022. It involves sustained ground combat and long-range strikes, including missiles and drones, and has caused extensive civilian harm, displacement and damage to civilian infrastructure.

facts.label: Origins
facts.value: The conflict’s modern phase began in 2014, when Russia occupied Crimea and hostilities began in Ukraine’s Donetsk and Luhansk regions; the United Nations General Assembly affirmed Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders and said the 16 March 2014 Crimea referendum could not alter Crimea’s status.

facts.label: Full-scale invasion
facts.value: The United Nations Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine states that Russian armed forces launched a full-scale armed attack on Ukraine on 24 February 2022.

facts.label: Geographic scope
facts.value: Hostilities affect Ukraine, including occupied territory and areas under Ukrainian government control; the war’s effects also extend beyond the front through long-range weapons and cross-border drone and missile incidents.

facts.label: International legal position
facts.value: On 2 March 2022, the UN General Assembly adopted resolution A/RES/ES-11/1, deploring Russia’s aggression against Ukraine and demanding that Russia immediately, completely and unconditionally withdraw its military forces from Ukraine’s internationally recognized borders. On 16 March 2022, the International Court of Justice indicated provisional measures directing Russia to suspend the military operations it had commen

facts.label: Humanitarian impact
facts.value: UNHCR’s 2026 planning appeal says the war has continued to produce acute humanitarian and protection needs in Ukraine and among refugees in Europe; it recorded 5.86 million refugees from Ukraine globally and 3.7 million internally displaced people as of December 2025.

event_overview.title: About Iran War
event_overview.subject: Iran War
event_overview.summary: “Iran War” is a shorthand for the 2026 armed conflict centered on direct U.S.-Iran hostilities, Iranian attacks and alleged attacks involving states around the Persian Gulf, and disruptions to maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. The United States calls its campaign Operation Epic Fury and says it began to protect U.S. forces, regional partners and navigation; Iran has described the U.S. and Israeli actions as unlawful aggression.

facts.label: Start of direct U.S. operation
facts.value: U.S. Central Command says Operation Epic Fury against Iran began on February 28, 2026, at the President’s direction. In a March 10 letter to the UN Security Council, the United States said it had commenced combat operations on February 28 in cooperation with Israel.

facts.label: Parties and regional reach
facts.value: The conflict directly involves the United States and Iran, with the United States describing Israel as an ally in its initial operations. UN Security Council resolution 2817 (2026) addressed attacks attributed to Iran against Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Jordan.

facts.label: Strategic waterway
facts.value: The Strait of Hormuz lies between Iran and Oman and connects the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea. It is a major oil and liquefied-natural-gas transit chokepoint, so threats to shipping there can have wider energy-market effects.

facts.label: Competing legal positions
facts.value: The United States notified the Security Council that it was acting in self-defense under Article 51 of the UN Charter. Iran has told the Council that the U.S. and Israeli campaign constituted aggression and that subsequent Iranian measures were self-defense; these are opposing state positions, not a judicial determination.

facts.label: U.S. constitutional and statutory contex
facts.value: Under the War Powers Resolution, U.S. policy is that the collective judgment of Congress and the President should apply to the introduction and continued use of U.S. armed forces in hostilities; the statute identifies a declaration of war, specific statutory authorization, or a national emergency created by attack as bases for introducing forces into hostilities.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers a limited set of developments from July 22-27, 2026—military threats, congressional war-powers action, shipping and oil-market pressure, Houthi claims, and ceasefire diplomacy—not the conflict’s full origins, all operations, or its eventual outcome.

stories.title: Iraq Confirms Origin of Attack on Saudi Pipeline Amid Militia Denials
stories.summary: Iraq's government has confirmed that an attack on a key Saudi pipeline originated from its territory, despite denials from an umbrella group of Iran-backed militias. The Iraqi authorities have pledged to investigate the incident and have dismissed two senior officials in connection with the attack. Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia has stated it will not retaliate and is urging Iraq to take necessary measures against the militias.

This escalation comes amid ongoing tensions in the region and rising oil prices.

event_overview.title: About Iran War
event_overview.subject: Iran War
event_overview.summary: “Iran War” is a shorthand for the 2026 armed conflict centered on direct U.S.-Iran hostilities, Iranian attacks and alleged attacks involving states around the Persian Gulf, and disruptions to maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. The United States calls its campaign Operation Epic Fury and says it began to protect U.S. forces, regional partners and navigation; Iran has described the U.S. and Israeli actions as unlawful aggression.

facts.label: Start of direct U.S. operation
facts.value: U.S. Central Command says Operation Epic Fury against Iran began on February 28, 2026, at the President’s direction. In a March 10 letter to the UN Security Council, the United States said it had commenced combat operations on February 28 in cooperation with Israel.

facts.label: Parties and regional reach
facts.value: The conflict directly involves the United States and Iran, with the United States describing Israel as an ally in its initial operations. UN Security Council resolution 2817 (2026) addressed attacks attributed to Iran against Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Jordan.

facts.label: Strategic waterway
facts.value: The Strait of Hormuz lies between Iran and Oman and connects the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea. It is a major oil and liquefied-natural-gas transit chokepoint, so threats to shipping there can have wider energy-market effects.

facts.label: Competing legal positions
facts.value: The United States notified the Security Council that it was acting in self-defense under Article 51 of the UN Charter. Iran has told the Council that the U.S. and Israeli campaign constituted aggression and that subsequent Iranian measures were self-defense; these are opposing state positions, not a judicial determination.

facts.label: U.S. constitutional and statutory contex
facts.value: Under the War Powers Resolution, U.S. policy is that the collective judgment of Congress and the President should apply to the introduction and continued use of U.S. armed forces in hostilities; the statute identifies a declaration of war, specific statutory authorization, or a national emergency created by attack as bases for introducing forces into hostilities.

event_overview.title: About Iran War
event_overview.subject: Iran War
event_overview.summary: “Iran War” is a shorthand for the 2026 armed conflict centered on direct U.S.-Iran hostilities, Iranian attacks and alleged attacks involving states around the Persian Gulf, and disruptions to maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. The United States calls its campaign Operation Epic Fury and says it began to protect U.S. forces, regional partners and navigation; Iran has described the U.S. and Israeli actions as unlawful aggression.

facts.label: Start of direct U.S. operation
facts.value: U.S. Central Command says Operation Epic Fury against Iran began on February 28, 2026, at the President’s direction. In a March 10 letter to the UN Security Council, the United States said it had commenced combat operations on February 28 in cooperation with Israel.

facts.label: Parties and regional reach
facts.value: The conflict directly involves the United States and Iran, with the United States describing Israel as an ally in its initial operations. UN Security Council resolution 2817 (2026) addressed attacks attributed to Iran against Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Jordan.

facts.label: Strategic waterway
facts.value: The Strait of Hormuz lies between Iran and Oman and connects the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea. It is a major oil and liquefied-natural-gas transit chokepoint, so threats to shipping there can have wider energy-market effects.

facts.label: Competing legal positions
facts.value: The United States notified the Security Council that it was acting in self-defense under Article 51 of the UN Charter. Iran has told the Council that the U.S. and Israeli campaign constituted aggression and that subsequent Iranian measures were self-defense; these are opposing state positions, not a judicial determination.

facts.label: U.S. constitutional and statutory contex
facts.value: Under the War Powers Resolution, U.S. policy is that the collective judgment of Congress and the President should apply to the introduction and continued use of U.S. armed forces in hostilities; the statute identifies a declaration of war, specific statutory authorization, or a national emergency created by attack as bases for introducing forces into hostilities.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers a limited set of developments from July 22-27, 2026—military threats, congressional war-powers action, shipping and oil-market pressure, Houthi claims, and ceasefire diplomacy—not the conflict’s full origins, all operations, or its eventual outcome.
